summary: Reviewed 2 files: src/server/routes/workspaces.ts (modified) and src/orchestration/workspace-health.ts (dependency). 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium findings. 2 Low/Info items noted (pre-existing patterns, not introduced by this WP). Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: Low/Info — A05 (Security Misconfiguration): projectId and workspaceId URL params are echoed verbatim in 404 error messages (e.g., 'Project "${projectId}" not found.'). For a local CLI-only tool this is acceptable, but would warrant a review for a public API. Pre-existing pattern throughout this file — not introduced by the health endpoint.

Low/Info — A01 (Broken Access Control): The workspaceFolder() helper constructs filesystem paths from URL params without explicit path-segment sanitization (e.g., no rejection of '..' segments). In practice, the data-layer gates (projectManager.getById → undefined → 404; workspaceManager.getById → undefined → 404) prevent the filesystem path-building code from being reached with malicious IDs. The new health endpoint uses this helper identically to the pre-existing withInitialized() helper. Defense-in-depth improvement would be to add an explicit assert that resolved path starts with appConfig.projectsFolder — but this is not a new risk introduced by this WP and does not rise to Medium.

No new security surface introduced. All OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed: A01 — data-layer gates prevent path traversal; A02 — no crypto ops; A03 — no injection vectors (no SQL, no OS commands, no templates); A04 — read-only, side-effect-free design; A05 — error messages echo IDs (pre-existing, acceptable for local tool); A06 — no new dependencies; A07 — no auth layer changes; A08 — no deserialization of untrusted data; A09 — error logging via ErrorLogManager consistent with other routes; A10 — no URL fetching, no SSRF surface.
